name: linked-single-radix7-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-7 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: gaussian-splat-blended-over-an-authored-imageblock
rationale:
First coverage of air.exp.f16, whose 121 case-less corpus sources are the largest uncovered count among the half-width transcendentals -- and half is the width at which fast::, precise:: and the unqualified Metal spelling agree, so the exact byte comparison survives it where the float-width families do not.

The AIR is one splat of a software Gaussian-splat rasterizer: it weights the incoming fragment colour by exp(-dot(uvGaussian, uvGaussian)) and blends the result over a custom imageblock that carries both the accumulated colour and a depth. A fragment case cannot choose its varyings -- the generated fullscreen observer fixes them -- but it can choose the imageblock, and at the one rasterized pixel the harness supplies uvGaussian = (0.5, 0.5) and colour = (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0). That makes the weight exp(-0.5), whose correctly rounded binary16 value is 0.6064453125, and it is the exp that decides every byte compared.

The authored imageblock colour (0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.5) is what makes the case an imageblock case rather than an exp case: its alpha 0.5 is the blend weight the shader reads back, and its three distinct RGB values are the destination the result is added to, so a plane that failed to alias onto the AIR's own imageblock, or that aliased lane-swapped, cannot produce the answer. Every step stays exactly representable in binary16 -- halving is exact, and each final sum lands on its own ulp grid -- so the closed form is (0.401611328125, 0.276611328125, 0.214111328125, 0.80322265625), which is what Metal returns byte for byte.

The pass has no colour or depth attachment: the imageblock is the attachment, and the AIR declares no render target for a manifest to name.

name: an-attachment-read-but-not-written-feeds-three-ordered-fetches
rationale: A color attachment the fragment function reads but does not write (DESIGN D200): exf2_fetch_unwritten reads rgba32_uint attachments 0 (count) and 1 (tag) and writes only attachment 0, count * 3 + tag, wrapping. Three instances of the fullscreen triangle apply it three times in order, so lane k of each pixel ends at c * 27 + t * 13 mod 2^32 exactly when every fragment read attachment 1 as loaded, so it pins what Metal leaves in a bound color attachment the fragment function does not write: an earlier fragment that had changed attachment 1 moves the integer (Vulkan may write undefined values to a color attachment the fragment shader has no output for unless the attachment's color write mask is zero). Authored lanes wrap (0xFFFFFFFF - p, 0x80000000-based, multiplicative hashes). This case observes attachment 0.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-eight-simd-primary

name: residency-across-the-tile-edge-of-each-slice-of-a-sparse-2d-array-texture
rationale: D264.11's third item: a sparse 2D array texture whose slices are mapped in different tiles, so each slice's tile edge is measured. A sparse texture (D264) is made on Metal from a sparse heap of 16 KiB pages and mapped with MTLResourceStateCommandEncoder before the work, and on Vulkan as a sparse resident image bound with vkQueueBindSparse; only the mapped texels' authored bytes are uploaded. Each region is a whole number of tiles on every device that runs the case (an executor refuses a region that is not whole tiles of its device), so the mapped texels are the same wherever the case runs; each run prints its tiling. Texture 0 is a 256x64x2 r32_float 2D array with texel (x, y) of layer l = 100000l + 1000y + x + 1 (exact); slice 0 has x 0..127 mapped and slice 1 has x 128..255 mapped (each region 128 x 64, a whole number of Metal's 64x64 tiles and Vulkan's 128x128 block cut by the level's edge). Thread i runs probe i of buffer 0 (32 bytes: kind, x, y, layer, u, v, lodf, lod as u32 u32 u32 u32 f32 f32 f32 u32) and writes out[2i] = the raw bits of the probe's float4 value and out[2i+1] = (resident() ? 1 : 0, kind, i, 0x5A5). The output is pre-filled with 0xAB, so an unwritten word shows; the AIR has no loop. Kind 0 is sparse_read(uint2(x, y), layer, lod) of texture 0 (a 2D array, sampled, so a fetch), 1 sparse_sample through a constexpr nearest clamp_to_zero normalized sampler at the layer and level(lodf), 2 the same through a linear one, 3 sparse_gather (component x) through the nearest one at the layer (level 0). Coordinates of samples are given in texels and divided by (256, 64), exactly. Probes: 0..3 read (5, 7) and (200, 7) of layers 0 and 1; 4..7 read (127, 63) and (128, 63) of layers 0 and 1, beside the edge; 8 read (5, 64) of layer 0, past the height; 9 read layer 2, past the count; 10 and 11 linear at (128, 8.5) of layers 0 and 1, weight 1/2 on each side of the edge; 12 linear at (64.5, 8.5) of layer 1, unmapped; 13..15 gather at (128, 8) of layers 0 and 1 and at (200, 8) of layer 0; 16..18 nearest at (127.75, 8.5) and (128.25, 8.5) of layer 0 and (128.25, 8.5) of layer 1. Texture 0 is an out-of-bounds target of the texture form (D225).

name: kernel-lod-query-through-a-constexpr-clamp-past-the-last-level

name: bounded-dynamic-visible-table-clear-slot-two
rationale: The literal four-word size table [4, 0, 0, 0] bounds the only reachable loop: its induction starts at visible-table slot 2, increments once to 3, and exits because the masked first word minus one is exactly 3. One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, selects register 2 as the output, and writes that slot's exact float4 zero result to pixel (0,0). The linked _uber_clear body returns zero without dereferencing the otherwise required callback arguments.

name: matmul2d-int8-into-int32-nn-16x64x16-two-simdgroups-whole-tile
rationale: matmul2d over int8_t into int32_t (DESIGN D272), whose sums are exact, so any order gives Metal's answer: 16x64x16, no transposes, multiply_accumulate, execution_simdgroups<2>, device memory (function constant 0 = 10); 64 threads. A has extents (16, 16) and B (64, 16) (extent 0 innermost, packed), random int8 values; C, a cooperative destination, starts from c0 by coordinate (row stride 64) and out receives it by coordinate, so a word out never receives keeps 0x5A5A5A5A. The extents decide which products enter each element: the case shows what Metal does at a nn 16x64x16 two simdgroups whole tile. Loops bounded by the capacity and by 2048 threadgroup bytes.

name: half-conversion-under-linear-address-modes
rationale: How Metal converts texels to half under the address modes half-conversion-of-wider-texels-by-read-and-sample does not read. Four 16x16 half textures: rgba32_float values around half rounding boundaries (ties, ties plus or minus a few float ulps, the overflow edge, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, NaN, random), rgba16_unorm codes nearest a half tie with endpoints and random codes, and rgba8_unorm and rgba8_unorm_srgb with every code per channel. Lane i takes the pixel coordinate p of texel (i mod 16, (i div 16) mod 16) at its centre (even i) or offset by seeded fractions k/256, k in 1..255 (odd i), and per texture writes three linear samples widened to float: under repeat at p over the size plus (1, -2), under mirrored repeat at minus p over the size, and under clamp-to-zero at (1.125 p - 1) over the size, to out[12i..12i+11] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: custom-filter-passthrough-zero-state
rationale: A zero shader-state vector disables every optional texture, table, framebuffer-fetch, and dithering branch. The separately linked visible callback returns its incoming half4 unchanged, while zeroed mandatory globals and custom arguments keep every reachable access in bounds. The poisoned one-pixel half4 render target observes the exact linked fragment result.

name: imageblock-full-tile-scalar-plane
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.i16.f16 (24 case-less corpus sources). A 32x32 threadgroup -- one cell per thread at Metal's 1024-thread maximum -- stages a luma of x + 32 * y into its own imageblock cell and thread (0, 0) copies the whole tile to the texture. The slice names no size, so the region is the threadgroup extent and the copy is of all 1024 cells; this translator allocated a flat 512-cell array until 29927ea1 and refused the module for naming cells that did not exist, so nothing had ever executed a full tile. Every luma is a distinct integer below 1024 and therefore exact in binary16, so a copy that started at the wrong cell, walked the wrong row stride or wrote only the origin lands a value the derivation places somewhere else. The texture starts filled with -1, which no cell can hold, so an unwritten texel is visible rather than plausible.

name: imageblock-full-tile-two-channel-plane
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.i16.v2f16 (15 case-less corpus sources), over the same 32x32 tile as imageblock-full-tile-scalar-plane. This plane sits at byte 4 of the 8-byte cell and is two channels wide where the luma is one, so a slice that took its stride or its offset from the cell rather than from the plane cannot satisfy both cases. Each cell holds (x / 2, y / 4): the two axes scale differently, so a transposed or row-shifted copy lands a pair that exists nowhere in the tile rather than one that exists elsewhere. Every component is an exact binary fraction, and the -1, -2 fill is a pair no cell can hold.

name: explicit-cube-gradient-minification-threshold-per-face-and-axis
rationale: A probe of the level of detail an explicit cube gradient selects (D283 family B), in a kernel: texture 0 is a cube and texture 1 a cube array of 2 cubes, rgba16_float 4x4, texel (x, y) of slice s holding 1 + x + 4y + 16s in every channel; the constexpr sampler minifies linearly and magnifies nearest over one level, so a sample is the nearest texel when the device's level of detail is at most 0 and the bilinear blend (1.25 above it, the directions lying a quarter texel past a texel centre in both face coordinates) when above. Lane i of 2016 takes face f = i % 6, gradient axis (i / 6) % 6 (+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z: buffer 0's float4s 12-17), the gradient as dP/dx or dP/dy ((i / 36) % 2, the other zero), and magnitude in[18 + i / 72].x (2^(k/4 - 3) to within 3%, binary fractions, k = 0..27: 0.125 to 2^3.75); it samples the cube and the cube array's layer 1 at two directions on face f with |major axis| 1 (in[f]: face coordinates (-0.125, 0.375), texel (1, 2); in[6 + f]: (0.375, -0.125), texel (2, 1)) and writes the four red channels to out[i] of buffer 1 (float4 elements, pre-filled with 0xAB). Where each face's and axis's sweep turns from the texel to the blend is that device's footprint of one texel. The AIR has no loop.

name: grid-stride-copy-that-skips-two-elements-in-four-regions
rationale: A 10x3 thread grid in 4x2 threadgroups tails in both dimensions, so the exact-thread plan runs all four of its regions: x full and x tail crossed with y full and y tail, each a separate local size and threadgroup base. The kernel rebuilds a flat index as threadgroup_position_in_grid.x * threads_per_threadgroup.x + thread_position_in_threadgroup.x and strides by threadgroups_per_grid.x * threads_per_threadgroup.x, so its result is a function of exactly the three facts a tail region changes. In the short x group threads_per_threadgroup.x is 2, which puts its base at 4 rather than 8 and its stride at 6 rather than 12; the consequence is that elements 8 and 9 are copied by nobody and keep the 0xEEEEEEEE poison. That hole is the signature - a lowering that reported the nominal four would fill them. Metal is the reference for this, because the shader is genuinely non-uniform-dispatch-sensitive; the twenty output words are pinned by hand from that model.

name: sign-of-zero-and-division-range-without-fast-math
rationale: The twin of sign-of-zero-and-division-range-under-fast-math (same inputs, same output layout; read that rationale): the same program compiled -fno-fast-math, for V5's comparison classes (D33, D113; the D110.7 residue). Without nsz, sign keeps D52.2's exact sequence, which returns -0 for -0. The module records air.compile.fast_math_disable, and its divisions carry no flags. The pair separates what fast math changes: a +0 from the step at w = -0 in this observation too would mean it is not fast math that produces it. Divisors past 2^126 that answer the exact quotient here but 0 in the twin would place the flush in fast math.

name: softplus-saturating-arms-in-one-texel
rationale: The one in-bounds invocation evaluates softplus on four components that all land on an exactly representable answer, so the observation needs no transcendental precision agreement. Components 0 and 1 (-1e30 and -100) drive air.fast_exp.v4f32 to zero or a subnormal that 1.0 absorbs, so air.fast_log.v4f32 answers exactly 0. Components 2 and 3 (100 and FLT_MAX) overflow the exponential past ln(FLT_MAX)=88.72 to +inf, the logarithm stays +inf, and the module's own exponent-mask test (bits & 0x7fffffff == 0x7f800000) selects the untransformed input, so those components must read back as exactly 100 and FLT_MAX. Both arms of that select therefore execute in one dispatch, and every written texel is exact.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two

name: composite-one-pixel-whose-three-lanes-split-on-the-half-alpha-test
rationale:
air.fast_saturate.v4f32 and air.convert.f.v3f32.u.v3i1 had no authored case between them; 56 corpus sources sit behind the pair. The host is a fragment blend - two texture samples fed through a saturate, an alpha composite and a per-channel hard-light with a half-alpha predicate.

A fragment case cannot choose its varyings, and this shader's three stage-ins are two unused float4s and the uv it samples with. Both textures are 1x1 with clamp-to-edge addressing, so whatever uv the harness interpolates and whatever the luma dot of the irrational Rec.709 coefficients comes out as, both samples return their single texel: the case is driven entirely by the two texels and the uniform block, which are authored.

The uniform offset is chosen so the saturate has to decide at both ends and neither - the three lanes going in are 1.25, -0.25 and 0.375. The composite then puts the three colour lanes at 0.875, 0.125 and 0.3125 against a half-alpha of 0.3125, so the boolean vector the convert turns into floats is true, false, true, with the third lane sitting exactly on the >= boundary; the mix that consumes it therefore takes a different branch in each lane and a collapsed predicate cannot pass. Every constant is a dyadic with at most ten fractional bits, so each product is exact and it does not matter whether the fast-math multiply-adds contract into fma. The four output floats were derived by hand and then re-derived by an independent evaluation of the AIR; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.
